A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PixelVLA. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison; internal reporting inconsistencies are identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original PixelVLA simulation results on SimplerEnv and LIBERO, component ablations, environmental-variation tests, and detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for fine-tuned OpenVLA and π0 baselines in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The architecture, L1 objective, and two-stage training remain substantially the same. However, v1 Section 4.3 specifies 256-bin action discretization, while v2 explicitly replaces this description with direct continuous prediction. v2 Appendix A.3 still specifies 256 bins, preventing a reliable distinction between an actual procedure change and an incomplete correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use Fractal and Bridge v2, Pixel-160K, and LIBERO-Pixel, with the same SimplerEnv robot/task coverage and four LIBERO suites. The additional baseline comparisons introduce no new dataset, task, or environment.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add OpenVLA-SFT and π0-SFT alongside the retained comparators. OpenVLA fine-tuning already appeared as +FT in v1's Google VA ablation, but its participation in the main comparisons and the π0-SFT comparator are additions.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 adds controls that fine-tune OpenVLA and π0 on Fractal and Bridge before comparison. The previously specified benchmark metrics, camera view, image resolution, action chunk length, training steps, and LoRA ranks otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 4 match, as do Figure 4's environmental-variation tests. The added explanations of drawer-task degradation and long-horizon performance introduce no additional diagnostic experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages without repeated-run counts, seed information, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds SFT baseline results and changes π0's Google VM average from 54.5 to 58.8 in Table 1. Existing PixelVLA, LIBERO, ablation, and appendix scores are retained. The new OpenVLA-SFT VA average of 38.6 conflicts with the 37.0 average for the same three task values in Table 4.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) retain the same likelihood factorization, masked feature aggregation, and L1 objective. Expanded encoder explanations introduce no substantive mathematical reformulation, theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same PixelVLA and Pixel-160K contributions, pixel-level understanding and multimodal prompting claims, headline 10.1%–28.7% improvement, and 1.5% pretraining-cost claim.

C2.justification: v2 attributes LIBERO-Long gains to action chunking and reduced discretization errors, and the drawer-task drop to catastrophic forgetting and task sensitivity, without new diagnostic evidence. New Appendix A.5 identifies limitations involving 3D inputs and advanced prompts and acknowledges the need for real-world robot validation.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 newly specify coordinate and prompt-type embeddings, Llama 2–7B for object extraction, expanded gripper bounding boxes, and script-plus-human mask filtering. These elaborate existing components without establishing changed implementation. The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a project-page address; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive Visual Prompting in VLMs discussion covering Shikra, Ferret, Ferret-v2, LocVLM, and related grounding work. Together with new PixelLM and OMG-LLaVA references in the introduction, this substantially broadens positioning beyond v1's VLA and instruction-tuning discussion. TinyVLA and the cited lifelong text-to-image work are removed.

P1.justification: v2 renames the visual prompting encoder to visual prompt-aware encoder, expands selected method and interpretation paragraphs, and adds acknowledgments and a limitations subsection. Affiliations and several textual errors are updated, while the overall section order and narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to separate pixel-mask and visual-prompt pathways, and Figure 5's episode illustration is revised. Tables 1–2 gain rows; the LIBERO and ablation tables exchange numbers, with the ablation table moved beside Section 5.4. Other changes mainly concern placement and caption corrections.

improvement.justification: Additional fine-tuning controls, clearer implementation descriptions, broader grounding-related context, and explicit limitations modestly improve assessment and reproducibility. The gains are limited by the unresolved action-discretization contradiction between Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3 and the new OpenVLA-SFT average inconsistency between Tables 1 and 4. Benchmark coverage and the central PixelVLA results remain unchanged.
